samehKasem.name: Dr. Sameh Kasem
samehKasem.summary: An Arabic-first medical portal for a consultant in brain, nerve and spine surgery — designed to turn search traffic into booked consultations.
highlights: CMS dashboard for patient reviews and procedure updates
samehKasem.caseStudy: Both locales are statically generated with next-intl, so every page ships as pre-rendered HTML with hreflang alternates and localized metadata. Medical schema markup targets condition and procedure searches, while the clinic team manages reviews and procedures from a Supabase dashboard — no developer needed.

mohamedSamy.name: Dr. Mohamed Samy
mohamedSamy.summary: A media-rich hub for a gastroenterology, endoscopy and liver consultant, built around videos, articles and patient cases.
highlights: Direct WhatsApp routing for instant patient inquiries
Video galleries and patient case studies
Dynamic CMS for medical articles and case studies
mohamedSamy.caseStudy: Articles and medical cases are managed in Supabase and published as statically rendered pages, each with its own metadata and Article structured data. The video gallery and one-tap WhatsApp routing keep patients a single tap away from the clinic.

mahmoudHassaan.name: Dr. Mahmoud Hassaan
mahmoudHassaan.summary: A high-conversion landing experience for a surgical oncology consultant, with a calm glassmorphism UI that builds trust from the first scroll.
highlights: Conversion-focused layout with persistent booking CTAs
mahmoudHassaan.caseStudy: Every page is generated at build time and served from Vercel's edge network. The glass effects are pure CSS with no runtime UI library, fonts are self-hosted through next/font, and content updates flow in from Supabase.

topPower.name: Top Power
topPower.summary: A full-featured corporate platform for an MEP engineering supplier, turning a fire-protection product catalog into a client-acquisition engine.
highlights: Client-acquisition workflows with call and WhatsApp routing
CMS-driven product, catalog and blog modules
Lighthouse 100 in SEO, Accessibility & Best Practices
topPower.caseStudy: Products, catalog and blog are CMS-driven from Supabase and rendered as static pages with Product and Organization structured data, with responsive images served through Supabase image transformations.

About.title: One developer, accountable for your project from first call to launch
bio: I'm Mohamed Ali, a full-stack engineer working across the .NET and Next.js ecosystems. Twenty-plus websites in, I've learned that clients don't buy frameworks — they buy more bookings, more inquiries and less hassle.

So every site I ship is built mobile-first, set up properly for Google from day one, and comes with a dashboard simple enough to update without calling a developer. You work with one person who designs, builds, launches and supports it — and who answers on WhatsApp.

Process.title: A clear path from first call to launch
Process.subtitle: No surprises: at every step you know what happens next, when, and what you receive.

call.title: Discovery call
call.description: We talk through your goals, audience and must-haves. You get a written quote and timeline before anything starts.

plan.title: Plan & design
plan.description: Page structure, content and interface design in Arabic and English — agreed before a line of code is written.

build.title: Build with live preview
build.description: Watch the site come together on a private preview link; your feedback is applied as we go.

launch.title: Launch
launch.description: Domain connected, SEO configured, site submitted to Google Search Console and speed-tested before handover.

support.title: Training & support
support.description: A walkthrough of your dashboard so you can edit content yourself, plus support after launch.

edit.q: Can I update the content myself?
edit.a: Yes. Every project includes a dashboard where you edit text, images, articles, reviews or products — no code and no developer needed.

own.a: Completely. The domain, hosting and source code are set up under your own accounts, so you're never locked in.

time.a: It depends on scope: a focused landing page usually takes 1–2 weeks, and a full website with a dashboard 3–5 weeks. You get an exact timeline together with the quote.

cost.q: How much does a website cost?
cost.a: Pricing depends on the number of pages and features. After a short call you receive a clear written quote — no hidden costs.

google.q: Will my site show up on Google?
google.a: Every site ships with technical SEO done right: speed optimisation, structured data, sitemaps and Search Console setup. Rankings also depend on competition and content, and I'll tell you honestly what to expect.

after.a: You get support after launch for fixes and small adjustments, and I'm available for new features or ongoing maintenance whenever you need them.
